name: Chris Pappas
subject: I know what honest work looks like. Sununu doesn't.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
| | |
---
Friend,
[
](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/14771?refcode=jtk1098-bu-nd&t=1&akid=11236%2E400544%2EcAhXr7)
Josh Rogers/NHPR
In the GOP primary debate, John Sununu told a roomful of Republicans he's running for Senate to send me back to "bussing tables” at my family’s “chicken restaurant."
He meant it as an insult. As if the people who work in restaurants — who cook your food, clear your plates, keep family businesses that are the heart of our state alive — have something to be embarrassed about.
**I’m not embarrassed. I’m proud.
**
My family opened our restaurant over 100 years ago. I know what a 65-hour week feels like because I've worked one. I know what it means to show up every day, work hard, and treat the people around you like they matter — because they do.
**John Sununu has never had to work hard a day in his life.** He was born into the Sununu political dynasty. His family's "business" isn't a restaurant serving New Hampshire families. It owns a literal gold mine in Azerbaijan that sells minerals to China.
That's what John Sununu calls “honest work.”
New Hampshire workers deserve a senator who knows what a hard day's labor actually looks like — who fights for small business owners, for restaurant workers, for every family just trying to make ends meet. John Sununu is running to protect people like himself. **I'm running for everyone else.**
He showed us who he is with these elitist comments. Now let’s make sure he doesn’t represent us. **[If you can, please split a donation between my campaign and Deb Haaland's.](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/14771?refcode=jtk1098-bu-nd&t=2&akid=11236%2E400544%2EcAhXr7)**

body:
My mission has always been to make life affordable for working families, and that doesn’t stop now.
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/9?t=1&akid=41519%2E3422442%2EUmBXPZ)
Dear Peter,
I wanted to share some updates with you on my future and what I’ve been up to.
First, it was the honor of a lifetime to represent California in Congress and to earn the support of so many of you in my campaigns for Senate and Governor. I’m incredibly proud of what we accomplished together.
Now comes the exciting part: what’s next.
One thing that’s always been a constant from when I was a little kid to now is a love of reading. During the pandemic, I started a book club in Irvine that is still going strong years later. Now, I want to share my passion for books with you. **That’s why I’m launching @KatiePorterTurnsThePage on Instagram!**
It’s partly a reference to a new chapter in my life, but also something I do a lot—turn the page when I’m reading. **[If you’re on Instagram, follow @KatiePorterTurnsThePage for book recommendations, reading ideas, and author content.](https://www.instagram.com/katieporterturnsthepage/)**
[](https://www.instagram.com/katieporterturnsthepage/)
[Follow @KatiePorterTurnsThePage](https://www.instagram.com/katieporterturnsthepage/)
I’m excited to share my favorite books with you, but that doesn’t mean I’m done with public service. My mission has always been to make life affordable for working families, and that’s not changing.
I will continue to engage in policy debates, help people learn how government works, and lift up candidates who will fight for everyday Americans.
That’s why **I’m continuing Truth to Power PAC** , my organization dedicated to supporting candidates who will lower costs, hold the powerful accountable, and get corporate money out of politics.
While I’m taking a step back from being a candidate myself, this fight is far from over. **[If you’re able, can you chip in $5 to Truth to Power PAC to support our work?](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20260724_1_ak.XkZd-b&refcode=em20260724-41519&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=41519%2E3422442%2EUmBXPZ)**
[Donate ›››](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20260724_1_ak.XkZd-b&refcode=em20260724-41519&t=21&akid=41519%2E3422442%2EUmBXPZ)
Thank you for being with me,
Katie Porter

Former U.S. Congresswoman Katie Porter founded Truth to Power to support the campaigns of her fellow Democrats. Truth to Power supports candidates who will stand up to Donald Trump, fight to lower costs, and protect the environment. **[Donate ›››](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/truth-to-power-1?refcode=em20260724-41519&amounts=&t=22&refcode2=41519_3422442_UmBXPZ&akid=41519%2E3422442%2EUmBXPZ)**

On **July 22, 2026** , the U.S. House of Representatives voted on **H.R. 7008, the Stop Insider Trading Act**. The bill passed by a vote of **232-198** , with overwhelming Republican support and the support of a small number of Democrats. Every member of Connecticut's Democratic congressional delegation--including **Jim Himes** --voted NO.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/030fd1ec-16ea-4822-ad15-6294c9b80332?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/58d9b4a0-5bc8-4a22-ab8c-28c21c30ca17?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
That vote deserves the attention of every Connecticut voter.
Before entering Congress, Jim Himes spent approximately 12 years at Goldman Sachs, ultimately serving as a vice president. He then entered Congress in 2009 and now serves as the **ranking member --the highest-ranking Democrat--on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence**. That committee oversees the nation's intelligence agencies and activities.
Those two parts of his resume make his vote especially significant.
A former Goldman Sachs vice president who now holds one of the most sensitive intelligence positions in Congress voted against legislation intended to restrict members of Congress from purchasing individual stocks while serving in office.
Connecticut voters deserve to ask why.
Should members of Congress be allowed to buy and sell individual stocks while having access to confidential legislative briefings, sensitive economic information and classified intelligence that can move financial markets?
I do not believe they should.
As a physician, attorney and the Republican-endorsed candidate for Congress in Connecticut's Fourth District, I believe public office should never provide opportunities for personal financial advantage that ordinary Americans do not possess.
Private citizens who trade securities using material nonpublic information can face SEC enforcement and, in serious cases, criminal prosecution. Members of Congress, meanwhile, routinely receive confidential information about legislation, economic policy, government contracts, sanctions, emerging technology and international events that may affect publicly traded companies.
Even when no law is broken, the appearance of a double standard damages public trust.
That double standard must end.
**A Serious National-Security Concern**
This is not merely an ethics issue. It is also a national-security issue--and Congressman Himes's position as ranking member of the House Intelligence Committee makes that concern even more important.
The House Intelligence Committee oversees the nation's intelligence agencies and activities. As its highest-ranking Democratic member, Himes occupies a leadership position involving some of the most sensitive information handled by Congress.
Committee members can receive classified briefings concerning military operations, terrorism, cybersecurity threats, foreign governments, sanctions, intelligence programs and emerging technologies. Many of those subjects can have major financial consequences for publicly traded defense contractors, cybersecurity companies, technology firms, energy businesses and other industries.
> **This is not an accusation that any individual member has improperly traded on classified information. It is an argument that Congress should eliminate the opportunity, conflict of interest and appearance of impropriety altogether.**
The higher the office and the more sensitive the information, the stronger the ethical safeguards should be.
A lawmaker responsible for overseeing America's intelligence agencies should understand better than almost anyone why access to confidential government information must never create even the possibility of personal financial benefit.
The American people deserve representatives whose decisions are based exclusively on the interests of the country--not the performance of an investment portfolio.
If elected, I will support strong and enforceable legislation prohibiting members of Congress and their immediate families from trading individual stocks while the member serves in office. Members of Congress should be held to the same standards as the people they represent--and, given their access and authority, perhaps an even higher standard.
**Send a Message on August 11**
The Republican primary is about much more than selecting a nominee.
It is our opportunity to send a message to Connecticut Democrats that Republican voters are energized, paying attention and prepared to remain fully engaged through November.
A strong turnout demonstrates that voters demand accountability, transparency and higher ethical standards in Washington. A weak turnout risks sending the opposite message--that voters are disengaged and simply do not care.
Do not let the dog days of summer keep you home.
**Early voting runs August 3 through August 9. Primary Day is Tuesday, August 11.**
Primaries are often decided by a relatively small number of votes. That means your voice truly matters. Your vote can help determine the nominee, strengthen the Republican ticket and build the momentum needed to compete in November.
**If you believe Congress should play by the same rules as everyone else, make your voice heard.**
If you believe access to classified intelligence should never create the possibility of private financial advantage, make your voice heard.
**And if you believe Connecticut deserves accountable representation in Washington, make your vote count on August 11.**
Thank you.
**Dr. Michael Goldstein**
_Republican-Endorsed Candidate for U.S. Congress, Connecticut 's Fourth District_

I sat down with New York Times columnist Ezra Klein for one of the longest interviews I've ever done.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]
It's been a funny experience.
People suddenly seem fascinated by this idea that an auto repair and machine shop owner from Skamania County wound up in Congress. But honestly... I'm not sure I'm all that interesting.
I still wake up in the same house, work at the same shop with my husband and struggle to find child care. I still worry about whether small businesses can survive. I still believe if the government writes a rule that doesn't make sense, we ought to fix it.
The cameras leave. The work continues. Sometimes I think Washington, DC forgets that.
Politics has become so focused on the next headline that we've stopped asking whether anything actually works. I didn't run for Congress because I wanted to become famous.
I ran because I got tired of watching practical problems pile up while everyone argued about them. That's why I'm still in this fight.
If more people are paying attention now, I hope they're paying attention to that.
Because Congress doesn't need more personalities. It needs more people willing to roll up their sleeves.

body:
CA Seeks to Revive Failed Board Gender Quota

[INSIDE JW]

JUDICIAL WATCH SUES AZ GOV. HOBBS OVER ICE ‘KNOW YOUR RIGHTS’
WEBSITE

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84359&L=38298&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly95b3V0dS5iZS9KYjlDRVpEZXNLdz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=588dde598ffc71a7c4010dad44f03ff3a5ca7d38d6ec3b4a61bb1678ef688e00]

In October 2025, we filed an Arizona Public Records Law lawsuit
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84359&L=36414&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvanVkaWNpYWwtd2F0Y2gtc3Vlcy1hei1nb3YtZm9yLXJlY29yZHMvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=460dbf87bddfba47d6e84ec857cae179613ecf5495ac1012c9255c0cc2d458d9]
against Gov. Katie Hobbs for records regarding her office reportedly
ordering state police and the Arizona National Guard to withhold
cooperation from federal immigration enforcement authorities
(_Judicial Watch Inc. v. Office of the Arizona Governor_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84359&L=36435&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtb2ZmaWNlLW9mLWF6LWdvdmVybm9yLWNvbXBsYWludC0wMzkyMTcvXV8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=8c712df8666149f11af0047e518cc4363301c40fde9d6e0d9b590ccfdbf195af _(No.
CV2025-039217)).

Our investigation of her antics continues. We filed another Arizona
Public Records Law lawsuit
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84359&L=38274&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtaG9iYnMtaWNlLXdlYnNpdGUtY29tcGxhaW50LTAyOTQ1Ni8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=cfb1b9bae113411cf30bb44b75019a1d9f011c02c81176155e1d33d29efe4ac0]
against Hobbs for records regarding the costs and communications
associated with her administration’s launch of a “Know Your
Rights” web portal advising Arizonans on interactions with
Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and other federal law
enforcement officials (_Judicial Watch Inc. v. Katie Hobbs_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84359&L=38299&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtaG9iYnMtaWNlLXdlYnNpdGUtY29tcGxhaW50LTAyOTQ1Ni9dXz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=bace1fcfbacc8928c3bf8da6545a47f2312e8a1bf78a240ecc28c1292076ef6d _(No.
CV2026-029456)).

We sued in Maricopa County Superior Court after the Governor’s
Office failed to produce records in a February 2026 public records
request about the development of the “knowyourrights.az.gov
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84359&L=38275&F=T&drurl=aHR0cDovL2tub3d5b3VycmlnaHRzLmF6Lmdvdi9d4oCdP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=d7dbbcbe5c461cb26fd5fc6cc76aff9763e840e506c4ef77fd81ca4527ab06bb website, as well as documents
supporting claims made by the Governor’s Office regarding alleged
violations of Arizonans’ rights by federal law enforcement.

The request further seeks communications between the Governor’s
Office and immigration advocacy organizations and individuals,
including Aliento Education Fund, Arizona Center for Empowerment
(ACE), Living United for Change in Arizona (LUCHA), Proyecto Progreso,
Raquel Terán, Reyna Montoya, and Lena Avalos.

In a February 4, 2026, press release
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84359&L=38276&F=T&&hash=2ba0033deb76a7ac3a1cb94c71260ae9f021f47d30dd747e0a2ea7c691c5ed81],
Hobbs’s office announces the launch of the web portal “to inform
Arizonans of their constitutional rights when engaging with federal
law enforcement or in peaceful protests.” Hobbs states in a video
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84359&L=38277&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g/dj1uU1c5Q0M5dWxzUSZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=2eee07c28b388816126eef2e1495d9d45d743d3d194d747738d7b97e2c4cd7e5] included in the release,
which also appears on the website, “I share the fear and anger of
many Arizonans who, over the past year, have seen far too many
instances of federal agents denying us our right to peaceful protest
...”

The launch of the website follows Hobbs’s April 2025 veto
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84359&L=38278&F=T&&hash=664c31d805e83ec2d9296f5fbc5f5eea2492a41d65147adb6ee6def2c0dae3c8]
of the “ICE Act” (Senate Bill 1164
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84359&L=38279&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYXpsZWcuZ292L2xlZ3RleHQvNTdsZWcvMVIvYmlsbHMvU0IxMTY0Uy5wZGY/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=fb223dd5caad5f95c815e7ddd6f691fa690c2d38ebad6d6a73552ef6dd9ba17f]), which AZ
Senate President Warren Petersen described as “a reasonable,
commonsense proposal supported by Arizona sheriffs to ensure all
levels of law enforcement were working with the federal government to
enforce our laws and protect our citizens from harm.”

Governor Hobbs is using taxpayer resources to promote a website built
around claims about federal law enforcement, yet her administration
refuses to provide the public with basic information about its costs,
development, and the records supporting those claims.

CALIFORNIA SEEKS TO REVIVE FAILED CORPORATE BOARD GENDER QUOTA

A California court permanently enjoined California’s secretary of
state from spending taxpayer money to implement a law requiring a
certain number of women on corporate boards because it violates the
California Constitution's equal protection clause.

But Gov. Gavin Newsom’s secretary of state, Shirley N. Weber,
decided differently and launched a flawed appeal.

In response we filed a 90-page brief
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84359&L=38282&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2NyZXN0LXYtcGFkaWxsYS1yZXNwb25zZS0yNzU2MS0zMjIyNzYvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=567c01734949d572bd7c55639a1270b64013f63eb5a862b7313ca61fb07f2175]
in the California Court of Appeal, defending the trial court ruling
striking down Senate Bill 826 (SB 826), the state’s controversial
law requiring publicly held corporations headquartered in California
to meet government-imposed gender quotas on their boards of directors.
Our brief urges the Court of Appeal to uphold the lower court’s
decision because the law violates the California Constitution's equal
protection clause:

> After 27 days of trial, 16 witnesses, 174 exhibits, and a trial
> transcript that spans over 8,500 pages, the Secretary was unable to
> convince the trial court that SB 826’s gender-based quota
> satisfies one of the toughest standards the law imposes—strict
> scrutiny. The law has multiple failings, not the least of which is
> that it was never intended to remedy alleged patterns and practices
> of discrimination in the board selection processes of some 625
> publicly held corporations headquartered in California.

The trial court concluded that the state failed to justify the quota
under the constitutional standard required for laws classifying
individuals based on sex. California now asks the Court of Appeal to
overturn that ruling and revive the quota law.

We filed the gender quota lawsuit
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84359&L=14941&F=T&&hash=940ea46dac86642c5fcec7f30744aa336ec3f2f125441a72e6a2e057406fe871]
in Los Angeles County Superior Court in 2019 on behalf of three
California taxpayers. The lawsuit challenged the 2018 law, which
mandated every publicly held corporation headquartered in California
to have at least one director “who self-identifies her gender as a
woman” on its board of directors (_Robin Crest et al. v. Alex
Padilla_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84359&L=14906&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2NyZXN0LWV0LWFsLXYtcGFkaWxsYS13b21lbi1vbi1ib2FyZHMtY29tcGxhaW50LTI3NTYxLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=5a3c5e6a8b955a19e682bd7bef6aae16969f0c2b6757dab9bc614f4ebd01965e]
(No. 19ST-CV-27561)).

Our appellate brief argues that California abandoned many of the
justifications it previously relied upon to defend the law and now is
attempting to recast SB 826 as legislation intended to remedy
discrimination—an argument that failed at trial.

Our brief argues:

> The law was sold to the Legislature ... as a way to increase
> women’s representation on corporate boards, if not achieve gender
> parity, and thereby boost the California economy and protect
> taxpayers, shareholders, and retirees. Because gender parity,
> economic benefits, and protecting taxpayers, shareholders, and
> retirees have never been compelling government interests under
> strict scrutiny, the Secretary needed another justification for the
> law when it was challenged in court. But because the legislative
> groundwork for a “remedying discrimination” compelling state
> interest had not been laid—and never could be laid—that effort
> failed. It should have come as no surprise then that the Secretary
> was unable to defend the law’s gender-based quota, despite having
> every opportunity to do so.

The brief also asserts: “By several measures, the number of women on
the boards of California’s publicly held corporations was increasing
before SB 826’s passage ... ”

The trial court specifically rejected the secretary’s claim that the
purpose of SB 826 was remedying discrimination and found as a factual
matter that the actual purpose was “gender equity or parity,”
“gender balancing,” and getting “more women on boards.”

The brief also argues that the secretary cannot refute “that SB 826
is not actually remedial.”

She makes no effort to show that SB 826 was “designed as nearly as
possible to restore the victims of specific discriminatory conduct to
the position they would have occupied in the absence of such
conduct,” ... Indeed, “[t]he lack of any effort to limit the
benefits of a remedial scheme to those who actually suffered from
specific discrimination will be fatal to the scheme.”

The brief also argues, “SB 826 plainly is a quota, and a rigid one
at that.... The secretary’s own expert described SB 826 as a quota.
One legislative report called it ‘essentially a quota system for
private corporate boards.’”

Here, the trial court found no proof that California directly or
passively participated in California corporations’ unlawful
discrimination against women in board selection or that California
corporations even engaged in such discrimination. It also found that
SB 826 made no meaningful effort to connect the law’s quota to
identified victims of specific wrongdoing, among its many other
failings.

California continues to waste taxpayer dollars defending the
indefensible – an unconstitutional gender quota scheme imposed on
corporations that only serves to help corporations virtue signal about
hiring women for their boards through government-mandated quotas.

The trial court correctly concluded the state failed to satisfy the
demanding constitutional standards required for government
discrimination based on sex. The Court of Appeal should affirm that
ruling and reject California's attempt to rewrite the purpose of the
law after losing at trial.

In 2020, we filed a separate taxpayer lawsuit
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84359&L=26922&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvanctc3Vlcy1jYWxpLXF1b3Rhcy8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=7d6d3113c8364f266dfee2a9b9090aec4ca95984f9b1261af63d92bf0bf31432] in Los Angeles
County Superior Court challenging Assembly Bill 979, which Governor
Gavin Newsom signed into law on September 30, 2020. That law mandated
racial, ethnicity, sexual preference and transgender status quotas for
corporate boards. On April 1, 2022, the Superior Court issued a ruling
and opinion
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84359&L=27068&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvY2EtY291cnQtb3Bpbmlvbi1leHBsYWlucy1oaXN0b3JpYy1ydWxpbmcvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=8a03e88c95d24a7921ad1ac22ea1b641cd5a1cc7aef07ff05548f57c5c8f5e99]
striking down Assembly Bill 979’s quotas and granting a permanent
injunction prohibiting the secretary from spending taxpayer money on
the unconstitutional law.

FBI Received Faxes 'Claiming Credit' for TWA Flight 800

We have serious questions about a 30-year-old tragedy.

We received 415 pages
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84359&L=38261&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL3R3YS04MDAtZmJpLXJlY29yZHMtanVseS0yMDI2Lz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=1bf58a1c311371e05a01df7bf792bc84d28a03bf6d22923fdbefe5d91d7c0765]
of records in a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request from the
Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) which show the Bureau received
faxes claiming credit for the July 1996 explosion of Trans World
Airlines (TWA) Flight 800.

An FBI New York Field Office electronic communication
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84359&L=38262&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL3R3YS04MDAtZmJpLXJlY29yZHMtanVseS0yMDI2LXBncy0xNy0yMC8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=7a6f752a7998ca853e2d1ae0454f1537eb374b03704eb1531d96eefde0d3c2da]
in case file 265A-NY-259028 was issued on July 19, 1996, just two days
after the July 17, explosion of TWA Flight 800. The four-page document
was sent with “Immediate” priority to the “FBI Director,”
“All FBI Field Offices,” and “All Legats.” Titled “UNSUB(S);
EXPLOSION OF TWA FLIGHT 800, 29 MILES SOUTHEAST OF HAMPTON, NEW YORK;
JULY 17, 1996; AOT – IT – EOD; OO: New York,” it states: “FBI
headquarters is in receipt of faxes generated from Cairo claiming
credit.”

Boeing 747-131 was bound for Paris from John F. Kennedy International
Airport in New York City. All 230 people died, including 212
passengers and 18 crew members.

To mark the 30th anniversary of the TWA Flight 800 crash, Judicial
Watch released a special investigative documentary
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84359&L=38263&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly95b3V0dS5iZS81ZVlWa3N0bkh3WT91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=23d48a580da58e5c34b860579992d9f904591730c2293e99e7cb97afa58a891d] on social media.

In “Judicial Watch Investigates TWA 800 — 30 Years Later,” a
special edition of its “On Watch” series, Judicial Watch examines
the full record of the air disaster. The documentary includes
interviews with experts with extensive knowledge of the tragedy;
interviews with witnesses; FBI records we obtained by FOIA, including
the July 1996 teletype stating the Bureau received faxes from Cairo
claiming credit for the disaster; and publicly available documents.

The official explanation for the TWA 800 crash includes a
controversial CIA animation concluding that the middle fuel tank was
somehow ignited and caused the crash. The CIA production dismisses the
accounts of dozens of witnesses who saw a streak of light rise up to
the plane before it exploded.

The documentary covers:

* The human story — 230 killed, including 16 Montoursville,
Pennsylvania high-school French-club students.
* The FBI overriding the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB)
from the initial hours of the investigation.
* The NTSB’s unresolved theory of an ignition source (“most
likely” a short circuit, never located or recreated).
* How no Boeing 747s were grounded for blanket inspections or repairs
immediately following the 1996 explosion of TWA Flight 800.
* How no 747 before or since the July 1996 crash has ever suffered
the catastrophic explosion of TWA 800.
* The Central Intelligence Agency’s (CIA’s) nationally televised
“witness perception” animation — from an agency with no
aviation-accident role.
* The explanation by the FBI and NTSB that traces of explosive
materials found on recovered parts of TWA 800 were from a K-9 training
exercise.
* The 755 witness reports — 183 describing a streak of light, 96 of
those placing its origin at the surface — none permitted to testify.

clean_body: CA Seeks to Revive Failed Board Gender Quota [INSIDE JW] JUDICIAL WATCH SUES AZ GOV. HOBBS OVER ICE ‘KNOW YOUR RIGHTS’ WEBSITE [] In October 2025, we filed an Arizona Public Records Law lawsuit [] against Gov. Katie Hobbs for records regarding her office reportedly ordering state police and the Arizona National Guard to withhold cooperation from federal immigration enforcement authorities (Judicial Watch Inc. v. Office of the Arizona Governor [ (No. CV2025-039217)). Our investigation of her antics continues. We filed another Arizona Public Records Law lawsuit [] against Hobbs for records regarding the costs and communications associated with her administration’s launch of a “Know Your Rights” web portal advising Arizonans on interactions with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and other federal law enforcement officials (Judicial Watch Inc. v. Katie Hobbs [ (No. CV2026-029456)). We sued in Maricopa County Superior Court after the Governor’s Office failed to produce records in a February 2026 public records request about the development of the “knowyourrights.az.gov [ website, as well as documents supporting claims made by the Governor’s Office regarding alleged violations of Arizonans’ rights by federal law enforcement. The request further seeks communications between the Governor’s Office and immigration advocacy organizations and individuals, including Aliento Education Fund, Arizona Center for Empowerment (ACE), Living United for Change in Arizona (LUCHA), Proyecto Progreso, Raquel Terán, Reyna Montoya, and Lena Avalos. In a February 4, 2026, press release [], Hobbs’s office announces the launch of the web portal “to inform Arizonans of their constitutional rights when engaging with federal law enforcement or in peaceful protests.” Hobbs states in a video [] included in the release, which also appears on the website, “I share the fear and anger of many Arizonans who, over the past year, have seen far too many instances of federal agents denying us our right to peaceful protest ...” The launch of the website follows Hobbs’s April 2025 veto [] of the “ICE Act” (Senate Bill 1164 []), which AZ Senate President Warren Petersen described as “a reasonable, commonsense proposal supported by Arizona sheriffs to ensure all levels of law enforcement were working with the federal government to enforce our laws and protect our citizens from harm.” Governor Hobbs is using taxpayer resources to promote a website built around claims about federal law enforcement, yet her administration refuses to provide the public with basic information about its costs, development, and the records supporting those claims. CALIFORNIA SEEKS TO REVIVE FAILED CORPORATE BOARD GENDER QUOTA A California court permanently enjoined California’s secretary of state from spending taxpayer money to implement a law requiring a certain number of women on corporate boards because it violates the California Constitution's equal protection clause. But Gov. Gavin Newsom’s secretary of state, Shirley N. Weber, decided differently and launched a flawed appeal. In response we filed a 90-page brief [] in the California Court of Appeal, defending the trial court ruling striking down Senate Bill 826 (SB 826), the state’s controversial law requiring publicly held corporations headquartered in California to meet government-imposed gender quotas on their boards of directors. Our brief urges the Court of Appeal to uphold the lower court’s decision because the law violates the California Constitution's equal protection clause: After 27 days of trial, 16 witnesses, 174 exhibits, and a trial transcript that spans over 8,500 pages, the Secretary was unable to convince the trial court that SB 826’s gender-based quota satisfies one of the toughest standards the law imposes—strict scrutiny. The law has multiple failings, not the least of which is that it was never intended to remedy alleged patterns and practices of discrimination in the board selection processes of some 625 publicly held corporations headquartered in California. The trial court concluded that the state failed to justify the quota under the constitutional standard required for laws classifying individuals based on sex. California now asks the Court of Appeal to overturn that ruling and revive the quota law. We filed the gender quota lawsuit [] in Los Angeles County Superior Court in 2019 on behalf of three California taxpayers. The lawsuit challenged the 2018 law, which mandated every publicly held corporation headquartered in California to have at least one director “who self-identifies her gender as a woman” on its board of directors (Robin Crest et al. v. Alex Padilla [] (No. 19ST-CV-27561)). Our appellate brief argues that California abandoned many of the justifications it previously relied upon to defend the law and now is attempting to recast SB 826 as legislation intended to remedy discrimination—an argument that failed at trial. Our brief argues: The law was sold to the Legislature ... as a way to increase women’s representation on corporate boards, if not achieve gender parity, and thereby boost the California economy and protect taxpayers, shareholders, and retirees. Because gender parity, economic benefits, and protecting taxpayers, shareholders, and retirees have never been compelling government interests under strict scrutiny, the Secretary needed another justification for the law when it was challenged in court. But because the legislative groundwork for a “remedying discrimination” compelling state interest had not been laid—and never could be laid—that effort failed. It should have come as no surprise then that the Secretary was unable to defend the law’s gender-based quota, despite having every opportunity to do so. The brief also asserts: “By several measures, the number of women on the boards of California’s publicly held corporations was increasing before SB 826’s passage ... ” The trial court specifically rejected the secretary’s claim that the purpose of SB 826 was remedying discrimination and found as a factual matter that the actual purpose was “gender equity or parity,” “gender balancing,” and getting “more women on boards.” The brief also argues that the secretary cannot refute “that SB 826 is not actually remedial.” She makes no effort to show that SB 826 was “designed as nearly as possible to restore the victims of specific discriminatory conduct to the position they would have occupied in the absence of such conduct,” ... Indeed, “[t]he lack of any effort to limit the benefits of a remedial scheme to those who actually suffered from specific discrimination will be fatal to the scheme.” The brief also argues, “SB 826 plainly is a quota, and a rigid one at that.... The secretary’s own expert described SB 826 as a quota. One legislative report called it ‘essentially a quota system for private corporate boards.’” Here, the trial court found no proof that California directly or passively participated in California corporations’ unlawful discrimination against women in board selection or that California corporations even engaged in such discrimination. It also found that SB 826 made no meaningful effort to connect the law’s quota to identified victims of specific wrongdoing, among its many other failings. California continues to waste taxpayer dollars defending the indefensible – an unconstitutional gender quota scheme imposed on corporations that only serves to help corporations virtue signal about hiring women for their boards through government-mandated quotas. The trial court correctly concluded the state failed to satisfy the demanding constitutional standards required for government discrimination based on sex. The Court of Appeal should affirm that ruling and reject California's attempt to rewrite the purpose of the law after losing at trial. In 2020, we filed a separate taxpayer lawsuit [] in Los Angeles County Superior Court challenging Assembly Bill 979, which Governor Gavin Newsom signed into law on September 30, 2020. That law mandated racial, ethnicity, sexual preference and transgender status quotas for corporate boards. On April 1, 2022, the Superior Court issued a ruling and opinion [] striking down Assembly Bill 979’s quotas and granting a permanent injunction prohibiting the secretary from spending taxpayer money on the unconstitutional law. FBI Received Faxes 'Claiming Credit' for TWA Flight 800 We have serious questions about a 30-year-old tragedy. We received 415 pages [] of records in a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request from the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) which show the Bureau received faxes claiming credit for the July 1996 explosion of Trans World Airlines (TWA) Flight 800. An FBI New York Field Office electronic communication [] in case file 265A-NY-259028 was issued on July 19, 1996, just two days after the July 17, explosion of TWA Flight 800. The four-page document was sent with “Immediate” priority to the “FBI Director,” “All FBI Field Offices,” and “All Legats.” Titled “UNSUB(S); EXPLOSION OF TWA FLIGHT 800, 29 MILES SOUTHEAST OF HAMPTON, NEW YORK; JULY 17, 1996; AOT – IT – EOD; OO: New York,” it states: “FBI headquarters is in receipt of faxes generated from Cairo claiming credit.” Boeing 747-131 was bound for Paris from John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York City. All 230 people died, including 212 passengers and 18 crew members. To mark the 30th anniversary of the TWA Flight 800 crash, Judicial Watch released a special investigative documentary [] on social media. In “Judicial Watch Investigates TWA 800 — 30 Years Later,” a special edition of its “On Watch” series, Judicial Watch examines the full record of the air disaster. The documentary includes interviews with experts with extensive knowledge of the tragedy; interviews with witnesses; FBI records we obtained by FOIA, including the July 1996 teletype stating the Bureau received faxes from Cairo claiming credit for the disaster; and publicly available documents. The official explanation for the TWA 800 crash includes a controversial CIA animation concluding that the middle fuel tank was somehow ignited and caused the crash. The CIA production dismisses the accounts of dozens of witnesses who saw a streak of light rise up to the plane before it exploded. The documentary covers: The human story — 230 killed, including 16 Montoursville, Pennsylvania high-school French-club students. The FBI overriding the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) from the initial hours of the investigation. The NTSB’s unresolved theory of an ignition source (“most likely” a short circuit, never located or recreated). How no Boeing 747s were grounded for blanket inspections or repairs immediately following the 1996 explosion of TWA Flight 800. How no 747 before or since the July 1996 crash has ever suffered the catastrophic explosion of TWA 800. The Central Intelligence Agency’s (CIA’s) nationally televised “witness perception” animation — from an agency with no aviation-accident role. The explanation by the FBI and NTSB that traces of explosive materials found on recovered parts of TWA 800 were from a K-9 training exercise. The 755 witness reports — 183 describing a streak of light, 96 of those placing its origin at the surface — none permitted to testify. In our investigation of the TWA Flight 800 tragedy, in March 2026 we filed 13 FOIA requests across eight federal agencies, including the FBI (six requests), NTSB, CIA, U.S. Department of Justice Criminal Division, U.S. Navy, U.S. Coast Guard, National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)/Clinton Library, and National Reconnaissance Office (NRO). In May 2026, we announced a FOIA lawsuit [] against the CIA for records regarding the agency’s involvement in the investigation of the crash of TWA Flight 800, including the decision to produce a witness perception animation that purportedly demonstrated how witnesses could have mistaken the visual effect of the exploding aircraft for a missile launch. “Judicial Watch Investigates TWA 800 — 30 Years Later” can be viewed on YouTube here []. After 30 years, we forced the release of a previously secret FBI document that raises questions about TWA Flight 800. The mysteries around the crash deserve a renewed investigation, as our new documentary demonstrates. DESPITE RAMPANT FRAUD, U.S. GIVES KYIV $10 MILLION TO COMBAT HIV Yes, Ukraine is notoriously corrupt, but that doesn’t stop State Department bureaucrats with their hands on your tax dollars. Our Corruption Chronicles blog looks [] at one wasteful program. Although the Trump administration plans to drastically slash funding of HIV programs in the United States in the coming year, it is allocating $10 million to combat the sexually transmitted disease (STD) in Ukraine, which already gets an exorbitant amount of aid from American taxpayers. Congress has allocated an astounding $195 billion [] in spending to the war in Ukraine and though most of it goes to military causes a big chunk has gone to humanitarian projects rife with corruption. Judicial Watch launched an investigation after a federal audit [] exposed fraud in the government’s extensive Ukrainian humanitarian aid initiative and last year sued [] [ notoriously corrupt State Department offshoot known as U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) that disbursed some $35 billion in aid to the former Soviet republic since the Russian invasion in 2022. Some of that money went to failed HIV programs in Ukraine that were later involved in criminal activity, a point of concern that should stop the flow of U.S. taxpayer dollars. A few years ago, Judicial Watch exposed [] [ of the fraudulent Ukrainian HIV charities that received tens of millions of dollars from Uncle Sam as well as generous contributions from leftwing billionaire George Soros. It was known as 100% Life and its purported mission was to fight for the life of people living with HIV in Ukraine’s 25 regions. But the Ukrainian HIV charity also helped another group embezzle international assistance and authorities launched an investigation that exposed a broad illicit scheme. The head of 100% Life’s board of directors, HIV-infected activist Dmytro Sherembey, was also investigated. A year earlier he published a book about AIDS that promotes the legalization of sex work and illicit drug use without punishment. Long before the Russian invasion, corruption in Ukraine [ HIV patients of crucial medicine, according to various reports published by news outlets and international human rights groups. There is no indication that anything has changed as the U.S. announces the latest grant to help the eastern European nation combat an epidemic of HIV, which has reportedly intensified since the war began. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), which is part of the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), will distribute the $10 million award to help the war torn nation’s inadequate Public Health Center (PHC) and Ministry of Health (MOH) enhance life-saving assistance for HIV conditions. The objective is to ensure that targeted HIV testing, treatment, retention and prevention services are widely available, according to the grant announcement [] issued this month. “Since February 2022, the global HIV program in Ukraine has encountered unprecedented challenges,” the document states. “Amid the ongoing war, it’s been especially challenging to meet the expanding needs of people at higher risk for HIV. The destruction of Ukrainian health and other key infrastructure has created a substantial risk of service interruptions and devastating challenges in availability of life-saving services.” The money will fund innovative, data-driven models and interventions for high-risk HIV populations, community services that help the infected adhere to treatment and address gaps in availability and use of essential life-saving HIV prevention services, among other things. High-risk HIV populations are described as people who inject drugs and their partners, people in prisons and other closed settings, those with high-risk sexual behavior and their partners as well as the displaced. The U.S. counts community-based HIV testing, linking the infected with care and using social network testing strategies to find those infected as past achievements in combatting Ukraine’s HIV crisis. It also lists complicated access to high-risk HIV populations due to security reasons, patients dropping out of treatment and late HIV diagnosis as its biggest challenges. “Amid the ongoing war, it’s been especially challenging to meet the expanding needs of people at higher risk for HIV,” the CDC grant document states. “The destruction of Ukrainian health and other key infrastructure has created a substantial risk of service interruptions and devastating challenges in availability of life-saving services.” People at higher risk of HIV need even more intensive support since the war began, the CDC claims. JUDICIAL WATCH: FIGHTING FOR ELECTION INTEGRITY We are a preeminent national force for clean elections, as Micah Morrison, our chief investigative reporter, describes [] in Investigative Bulletin. In the fight for election integrity, Judicial Watch continues to notch voter-friendly victories across the country. In California, Judicial Watch sued the state for failing to maintain accurate voter rolls—a requirement of the National Voter Registration Act. The law requires the removal of most inactive voter registrations after two general elections. The numbers are astonishing. The JW lawsuit charges that California failed to remove 873,000 inactive voters from their registration rolls who have been inactive for more than two general elections. Sometimes a lot more: tens of thousands of the registrations have been inactive for over ten years. The lawsuit was filed on behalf of the American Independent Party of California and Don Wagner, an elected member of the Orange County Board of Supervisors who is running for California Secretary of State. Last week, the Justice Department filed notice that it intended to intervene in the lawsuit on behalf of Wagner and the Independent Party. Citing data from Judicial Watch’s original complaint, the Justice Department said in its Complaint in Interventio [ [] that California “does not comply with the NVRA’s requirement that the state conduct a general program of voter registration list maintenance that makes a reasonable effort to remove persons from the voter rolls who have become ineligible.” JW President Tom Fitton welcomed the federal move []. Dirty voter rolls can mean dirty elections. “The Justice Department is right following Judicial Watch’s lead and join our fight to clean up California’s dirty voting rolls,” Tom said. This isn’t Judicial Watch’s first election-integrity rodeo in California. In 2019, Los Angeles County settled a JW lawsuit [] that resulted in the removal of more than 1.2 million names from voter rolls. In April, Judicial Watch announced a historic milestone [ removal of six million ineligible names from voter rolls nationwide. In Colorado, 372,000 ineligible voter names were removed from voter registration [] lists following a lawsuit and settlement. In the settlement, Colorado agreed [] to a sweeping voter roll cleanup, with extensive follow-up and reporting. In Oregon, Judicial Watch reached a settlement [] in its federal lawsuit against the state. Oregon officials confirmed that 800,000 ineligible voter names are slated for review and removal from voter registration lists. In June, Judicial Watch came close, but ultimately lost, an election integrity case [] before the U.S. Supreme Court. Judicial Watch led the effort to uphold Election Day at the Court. We represented the Libertarian Party of Mississippi in the case, arguing that a single day for Election Day should be enforced and the counting of ballots that arrive after Election Day be prohibited. In our brief to the Court [], we argued that “the whole point of the federal Election-Day statutes is to set a single uniform day for the election. Allowing ballots to trickle in days or weeks after Election Day is antithetical to that basic goal.” In its July 2 ruling [], a closely divided Court declined to uphold a single, uniform Election Day. Tom called [] the 5-4 decision “astonishing.” But in January, the Supreme Court ruled 7–2 in favor of granting standing in a historic case filed by Judicial Watch [] on behalf of Congressman Mike Bost and two presidential electors. The case challenged an Illinois law allowing the counting of ballots received up to fourteen days after Election Day. The landmark ruling in the Bost case established an important principle, affirming the rights of a political candidate to bring election-ballot disputes to federal court. On January 6th, 2021, while rioters were breaking windows and beating police officers in the United States Capitol, Scott DesJarlais watched and chose to throw out electoral votes. Over 60 lawsuits were filed, remember? Guess how many were dismissed... just about every last one.
**DesJarlais didn 't care. He voted to override you anyway. [I'm running a race against this kind of corruption, and need your help today!](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/275080c9-edf7-4470-a9ff-a6bf05f7731b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Different Day, Same Fight. HELP HERE🚨](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/275080c9-edf7-4470-a9ff-a6bf05f7731b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Before Jan. 6th, he had already signed onto a Supreme Court brief trying to invalidate the votes of Georgia, Michigan, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin. Millions of American voters stood in line and trusted the process... and Scott DesJarlais tried to erase them with a legal stunt the Supreme Court threw out immediately.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/f1a59fc3-8e1d-43eb-8ddd-13b7e2304d22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This isn't a difference of opinion on tax policy or healthcare. A sitting member of Congress said "_the votes only count when my side wins, " _and he has upheld that MAGA loyalist standard for years.
**I come from a different place entirely.** I believe the ballot box is sacred and when Tennesseans vote, those votes deserve to be counted and respected full stop. I say cut the legal maneuvers, _**I believe in Rule of Law.**_
DesJarlais has been in Washington for 14 years and in that time he's learned one thing really well: how to protect himself and only himself. He's learned how to sign the right briefs and keep the right people happy, even when it means telling the voters of this district that their voice only matters when it's convenient.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/11754ef3-c34a-47f4-9c3f-e23a78f43f3e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

| Supporters and Friends,

George Washington was one of the finest military commanders our nation has ever produced. But did you know he actually lost more battles than he won?

He was a good general because he understood strategy, and that even when you don’t take the field on a particular day, staying in the fight, conserving your resources, and maintaining morale among your men can still win you the war.

That’s what I want you to remember. A battle is not the war.

Unfortunately, Tuesday did not go our way. But I’m proud that we had the thinnest margin of any state senate race on Election Day. That’s because of your efforts.

Thank you to everyone who joined me for door knocking, who placed a sign in their yard or business, who made a donation, or even just by reading this newsletter. And especially thank you to everyone who blessed me with their vote and their confidence in my ability.

This campaign was built around American sovereignty, constitutional principle, and the rule of law. I believe in these honored traditions as much today as I did yesterday.

That is why I end this campaign without despair or regret. The MAGA movement will continue under President Trump’s leadership.

And I will continue to work alongside him, as I have since 2015.

Thank you again for all you have given, and let us be inspired by George Washington’s example and keep up morale until the next fight.

Trump, meanwhile, is for a broader offensive and has threatened to seize Iranian funds to cover shipping losses as negotiations stall. ★★★ DOJ Sues Colorado Over Tuition The Justice Department against Colorado over its ASSET law, which grants in-state tuition and financial aid to illegal immigrants at public colleges and universities. Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward said the state is subsidizing education for illegal aliens at taxpayers' expense while denying the same rates to out-of-state American citizens, violating a 1996 federal statute. It marks the fourteenth such lawsuit the administration has brought, following courtroom wins in Texas, Kentucky, Oklahoma, and Nebraska. Democratic Gov. Jared Polis and Sen. John Hickenlooper , accusing the administration of reviving culture-war battles instead of fixing a broken immigration system. ★★★ Trump Returns to Press Dinner President Trump to the rescheduled White House Correspondents' Association dinner at the Waldorf Astoria, roughly three months after gunfire forced the evacuation of April's banquet in an alleged assassination attempt. Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt promised an she described as "unifying yet vicious," while the association framed the do-over as proof a free press will not be intimidated. Much of the Cabinet , though Melania Trump, Vice President JD Vance, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio will not. The Secret Service officer who helped stop the April suspect is expected to receive a special award. House Bans Stock Trades The House the Stop Insider Trading Act 232-198, barring lawmakers and their families from trading individual stocks. Speaker Mike Johnson called it a step toward restoring public trust. ★★★ Voter ID Standoff Trump's with Senate Republicans over the SAVE America Act, which requires proof of citizenship to register and photo ID to vote, and wants it enacted before the August recess. ★★★ Kids Online Safety Senate Commerce Chairman Ted Cruz will kids' online safety and artificial-intelligence bills in early August, including a version of the Kids Online Safety Act cosponsored by Sen. **Good morning!** On this day in 1878, notorious outlaw Black Bart robbed a Wells Fargo stagecoach in California, stealing less than $400 and a passenger's diamond ring and watch. A taunting poem signed "Black Bart" was found inside the recovered empty safe box. [See the poem here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOszAQBOCnMZ2RsxiMCxd_Q5e_vRIZvIRNDI7svSDe_pTo3uDqT5rRzNd1vHqKtN_--w0dL2nc8SgRmTGPz8S4M_m4-VLohZT9XjjTYwQFnVRGQjsGT_EcdRXcggjYVOguptfWaNWpanXGNtDBsuiuC7a3RhlcrO8A2uAnDaEi905TBtqLUqbp67YPelL9ZZqsnefGCq0wEKdc3xPtvOISz_TCXM9pq6JbmZ9FNP8EDAKG4zjqlQqnfL5dwMArFRn8KWmXvyJguH_HU0IrYJiinx9y8pnlZxwW6W-e9iq78DwoRiqdEVrdNk_x08l_Ourl4CcAAP__-5t9-w). Our question yesterday asking readers about their old-world skills brought in some great stories. We heard from readers who still split their own firewood every year, along with those who take pride in knowing how to change a tire, repair a fence, sew a button, sharpen a knife, can vegetables, bake from scratch, or tackle just about any household repair without calling for help. Some of the skills were a bit more uncommon, like the reader who made an effort to keep writing in cursive, the couple who built their own home (not paid to have it built, but _built_ it), and our favorite, the gentleman who calculates the square root of a number using pencil and paper every night, just to make sure he still can. For our part, it was great to see so much appreciation for being able to do things with your own two hands and brain. Could the health habits you swear by be built on dementia myths that scientists abandoned years ago? Many people are still making daily choices based on outdated ideas about the disease, and those false beliefs could be quietly raising their risk. Knowing the truth before symptoms appear may be the difference between protecting your brain and losing precious time. In today's episode of _The Flyover Podcast_ , Amy breaks down six dementia myths a neuroscientist says we all need to unlearn. So how many of the six are shaping your lifestyle, and what should you be doing instead? [Tune in here!](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykzz1ywyAQQOHTSJ01y48MKijSuHPalAwSi70JAg3s2PHtM8kVcoD3Zr6Pq78GylRu72FHx6n6gs-ekRmbPypjYQp5D73TA6mF0rnRl5cgzycwJzn7GCi_vB6jS4gS1YhOGKsXo-EM493NJiaRNkiASier57QIFTYhQetkrRrJ_d7AyFkAGGWn2Ua9ghXruizbppZBA0bi2qbPSoXvmPKrPrBNW93H7O7MRx_U2yAvg7w0XFsoccqvQV6OGvGbWxBjc_F4Us7Uz2bQcNsD5b-e_4V-OPkTAAD__2ePa2I)

## Trump Weighs 'Massive' Iran Strike
President Trump said he was [weighing a "massive attack"](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFutDAQhJ_GdCCzYAyFi7-hu79NiQws501sjOzl0OXpI_IK6UYa6RvN9_GYHpY87c__NqDhLU47XtkjM6bpiIw7k_XB5kwvpGT3zIm-JpDQlVKXoKbVkn9PbbGaDRGwKdDUum8H3cpOFs506zBIBTXqDTTq2Sqrln7blLYKeugLMjdNalC1lLrpK9Wv7Sz7ep6HYVmaQbQSV-KYqs9IOzvc_Du-MFVLDIU3jvnIovknYBQwXtdVLfu83KWA8UYLGKW-cytgPHN53ygvm0pOZzhKF1M4v0sXT3aUK8fBF8msx0XeU-60aOUzWPK_c_wnRy8DPwEAAP__jHx6cA) on Iran that would be "bigger than ever before" in the wake of Iran bombing military bases in Jordan. The threat came as the U.S. completed a 13th straight night of strikes on Iranian military targets, following Houthi terrorist strikes on two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, speaking at an Asian security conference in the Philippines, said [Trump's policy toward Tehran](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DHOozAQxfHTmI7IDAbjwsU2dNl2SzTAEGZjY2RPEuX2K_YKX_2kv_R7f-7THTnw8fiNkbxsaTroUwKJUJ7OJHQIY4hYCr-JMx5FMj8n0NDX2tbQTSty-E6mWv1GBNRW5Bs7GGeN7nW1-80OrVsaS8uKnYF56zdn3IZ2XshYYyr2V01b6BqtbTvcumE1sx6aeXZuWVqnjKaVJeXb38SH7LSFb3pTvi0pVsHvImdR7S8Fo4JRdto5hGtTMO4p0gVSMOIa-eAiGYXToWDs3NBDD7XkVzzry1a_Sh05sGD-1iiCy1PBWGW_nh8OgUtvldGPiPy_X8mPDnt7-BcAAP__ehqA_A) amounts to "a head for an eye" and that Iran "will pay a very heavy price for the things they're doing." Meanwhile, the U.S. and U.K. are [planning a conference](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2unDAQhZ_GdF4Z28tP4WKTiFQ3TYqUaMDDMrlmjGyzaPP0EXmF1N_R0Tnfr4_xAygQP3_Ahq4scWQ8c8BSMI17LMiFIGyQM72QEnAuiT5HrXQjVSv1ffRA4T3ayrsFUaOp0NVtZ_vWqkZVq9PQNDWYxSiw1vi7RT0t_gpA3yirKnJXm2r1vVaqNd3t3nk7qa6epr6fZ9MLq9BTien2OxKXFZfwji9MtzluVXBrKXsW5iH0IPRwnudty3wxoQdkeWShh-vUBWMKXughzzHu8sgS2MvjU-4BmImfkrhgYigUGYKcIy-YkGeUkWUuCajIuMg1pu34I_QAST4euvtaf5-EGeJMXphvXy6beOafmPYqOb-fFALlphVWPTeg8G93-S_ZL6f_BgAA__8i9ZV8) in London next week on protecting shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.
## Passengers Survive Fiery Seaplane Crash
A Kenmore Air seaplane [crashed and burst into flames](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OqzAQhZ_GdEaO-TEULm5Dl9tuiQZ7CLMxNrInQXn7FfsK2x3pSOfo-77u8x0oUHz8hx0tr2mOeJaAzJjnIzFGJgg7lEJvpAyxcKbnrJXupTJSd7MHCp-5rbxdETU2FdqbGdrRtKpX1Waxgwa9d03bKGPWftXgNTo9DIhL5_qK7LWmjO5uSplmqLvBt4sabssyjs41o2gVeuKU6-9EkTdcwye9Mdcu7VWwG_NRRPNP6Eno6TzP2i3lorh6oacrCj0VhCNAROkylE0erweyLOkVvSwIzAHlE-OeMkqgLPRUZeuPk0Kg0hvRqscOFH4_-U-i3lb_BAAA__9WjX-L) Thursday evening near Washington state's San Juan Islands after the pilot attempted an emergency landing, but all 10 passengers and the pilot somehow survived. The de Havilland DHC-3 Otter left Seattle's Lake Union around 4:30 p.m. bound for Roche Harbor. About 45 minutes later, the aircraft went down in Shallow Bay near Sucia Island, erupting into a fireball after hitting the water. [This video shows](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOpDAQBNCvMZmRMR4MgYNLyObSC1FjeqBvjY3cXtDs16_YX9ispJKeSvXvOT2BAsX1L-zoyitNES8OWArm6UgFYyEIOzDTiZQhcsn0MWmlO6ms1I9pAQrvyVSLeyFqbCt0je3NYI3qVLU57E1nDfR-aEyvZtQGvW8tDGowiNhU5G5NWf1olLJtXz_6xcyqb-Z5GLxvB2EULlRSrv8nimXDV3inE3Pt014Ft5VysGj_CD0KPV7XVZf96-6EHm9Z6FHZOxuhR0Y4AkSUPgNvyJKivIA3imtJUUII8gBmjCtmlvyZTzpR6LHKbjkuCoG4s8KodQcKPwPKr147nf4OAAD__7I5gVk) the fiery wreckage. The Coast Guard, local first responders, and nearby boaters pulled everyone aboard from the water. [One person was in critical condition](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOozAQxvGngc6RMQRD4eKadLn2SjQ2Y5hbYyPPbKK8_Sp5ha3_0qefvn_35Q6UKG9_4UAnsSwZn5xQBOtyFsEsBOkAZnogVcgslb4Wo82otFXmuqxA6bUM7eoiosG-RdfZaZjtoEfd7s72OvjRB7_GaDodZjOh1qOFCHOPQ2zJvde0NddOa9tPl-u0Dl5PnffzHEI_N4PGlaTUy_9CWXaM6VUeWC-hHG1yu8jJTf-nMbfG3E4sZ8J3asyNEc4EGVWAWl-UN9V1KlTgHVl5jKWi8t-V5Z0oS1ExwYGsSozqCbxT3qRkxQKCKhRgUd1HO5m2uvV8UkrEo20GvR1A6UOSX_34cOYnAAD__wliifA), with other injuries including broken bones and head trauma. The FAA and NTSB are investigating, and Kenmore, the nation's largest seaplane airline, canceled all Friday flights.
## List: Weekend Vs. Weekday Activity
Americans' TV viewing jumps by nearly an hour on weekends, rising from 2 hours and 20 minutes on weekdays to 3 hours and 16 minutes, according to a government [report on 2025 weekend activities vs. weekdays](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOqzAQRb8GOiNjDIbCxWvo8tot0WBPwmyMjexZUP5-lfzCdre4Okc6X7flBhQoPv7DjpbvaYl4lYDMmJcjMUYmCDuUQidShlg403NRUg1CGqH6xQOF16Jrb--ICrsabWtGPRktB1lvdsXJawlm1EYZ7MGptlODdC2uU-dUV5N906RRfSul6camH71e5diu6zQ5102VluiJU26-E0Xe8B5e6cTcuLTXwW7MR6m6f5WaKzVf19WcVH4gODiIIVDh97FS85YuATtmchCLKAdGL3hDyoJpR5GiuBCfHl5FnOWzMfpSqbnO1h8XhUBlMJWWjx0ofOz8p2SnVb8BAAD__9T_gvI). Television captures about half of all available leisure time on both types of days, suggesting Americans don't so much change what they do on weekends so much as how much time they spend doing it. Socializing more than doubles on weekends, adding roughly 29 minutes, while sleep climbs by nearly an hour. The data shows the Americans also spend nearly two additional hours on leisure and sports on the weekend. You can [see the full breakdown here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOqzAQRb8GOiNjDIbCxWvo8tot0WBPwmyMjexZUP5-lfzCdre4Okc6X7flBhQoPv7DjpbvaYl4lYDMmJcjMUYmCDuUQidShlg403NRUg1CGqH6xQOF16Jrb--ICrsabWtGPRktB1lvdsXJawlm1EYZ7MGptlODdC2uU-dUV5N906RRfSul6camH71e5diu6zQ5102VluiJU26-E0Xe8B5e6cTcuLTXwW7MR6m6f5WaKzVf19WcVH4gODiIIVDh97FS85YuATtmchCLKAdGL3hDyoJpR5GiuBCfHl5FnOWzMfpSqbnO1h8XhUBlMJWWjx0ofOz8p2SnVb8BAAD__9T_gvI).
